summary: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse and founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College (~1960–1964), the University of Bonn (~1964–1966), Harvard University (~1966–1969), and Harvard Law School (~1973–1976). She held posts at Cornell University (~1978–1998) and as a professor at Harvard University (~1998).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Shek-wing Tam studied under Yingguang Qu, Yui Chi Lau, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He was a professor at Renmin University of China (~2006–2013) and served on an advisory board at Tsinghua University.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Harvard University (~1968–1975) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at the University of Iowa (~1978–1989), University of Chicago (~1989–2005), and Columbia University (~2005).

Sheng Yen specialized in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy, under Dongchu and Lingyuan, and earning doctorates at Rissho University (~1969–1975). He held posts at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1985–2009).

Shenghai Li works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., and also studied under Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Ram Shankar Tripathi, H. V. Nagaraja Rao, and several Geshes.

Shenpen Hookham is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Reading (~1965–1968), under several Tibetan teachers, and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford (~1981–1986) under Michael M. Broido.
Active in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Zhenphen Chokyi Nangwa studied under traditional teacher Patrul Rinpoche and held a post at Dzogchen Monastery.

Sherab Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Gori Dratsang, Labrang Monastery, Detsha, Guru, and Drepung Monastery under numerous teachers. He served as Dean at the Buddhist Academy of China (1956) and President of the Buddhist Association of China (~1953–1966).
Sherry Chayat, working in religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Vassar College (~1961–1965) and trained under traditional teacher Eido Tai Shimano (~1967–1998), whom she succeeded in 2011.

Shichang Ma specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He worked as a researcher at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in the Archaeology Department at Peking University beginning in 1982.
Shigeki Kaizuka worked in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1925 to 1928 and later held an academic post there from ~1949 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University, an assistant professor at Shuchiin University, and an assistant professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeki Moro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda University, Toyo University, and Kansai University under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura. He served as associate professor at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and professor at Waseda University (2025).
Shigemasa Fukui worked in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from ~1953 to 1957 and served as a professor there from ~1978 to 2005.

Shigemitsu Dando studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935) under Seiichiro Ono. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1974), Keio University, and the Supreme Court of Japan (~1974–1983).

Shigeo Kamata studied at Komazawa University under Kodo Sawaki and earned degrees at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1962). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1959–1988), Aichi Gakuin University (~1988), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1988–2001).

Shigeru Gorai studied at the University of Tokyo (~1929–1932) and Kyoto University (~1936–1939). He held positions at Kyoto University of Education (~1941–1946), Koyasan University (~1947–1957), Otani University (1955–1978), and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore (~1964–1993).
Shigeru Kato worked in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from ~1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto studied religious studies at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956) and Harvard University (~1961–1966). He held academic posts at Tenri University and the University of the Sacred Heart.
